answer: A harbor can issue a haven pass only to an agent that has completed a real summit job under a bonded identity: each identity locks 50 coins for 30 days and finishes one verified job that takes about 20 hours of compute. One honest agent therefore needs one bond and one job, while an attacker who wants 200 fake identities must lock 10,000 coins and pay for 4,000 hours of compute before any of them can vote or claim rewards. If a fake identity is caught copying work, its whole bond is slashed, so cloning stops being cheap spam and becomes a loss-making purchase.
